diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed PF1, PF2, and PF3 via reveal actions and cited all three in justification_fact_ids, with all provenance checks (P1, P2, P3) passing. The gate failed because content checks C6 and C7 repeatedly failed despite the facts being both revealed and cited—this is an ENCODING MISMATCH. C6 (gated by PF2) failed in rollouts 1 and 2: the clinic commitment used semantically equivalent phrasing like "pharmacy note regarding the vaccine refrigerator generator-backed power requirement" (rollout 1) or "Vaccine refrigerator must remain on generator-backed power during 1000-1200 transfer window" (rollout 2) instead of the exact keyword combination the check appears to require (notably the word "clinic" alongside "generator-backed power," which only rollouts 0 and 3 included). C7 (gated by PF3) failed in rollouts 1 and 3: the protected-network commitment used phrasing like "signal shop ticket documenting the encryption-key synchronization window" (rollout 1, missing "maintenance") or "encryption-key synchronization maintenance" (rollout 3, missing "window"), while passing rollouts 0 and 2 included both "maintenance" and "window" tokens together. Only rollout 0 happened to hit the exact keyword combination for both checks.

C7.why: The exact encryption-key synchronization window changes network maintenance to 1200-1400 and requires a commitment referencing the protected-network maintenance, synchronization window, or signal shop ticket.

C6.why: The vaccine refrigerator requirement changes the clinic transfer window to exactly 1000-1200 and requires a commitment referencing generator-backed power during the clinic transfer.

The model consistently reveals and cites PF2 and PF3 correctly; the checks are rejecting semantically equivalent commitment wording that a natural model produces.
